instructions: Operator setup is incomplete: replace this paragraph with the approved project guidance, the delivery target, and what each configured command in this run actually builds, tests, delivers and reads back, before accepting work. Progress in this run is decided by the configured commands, not by anything a role writes: a stage that runs a command is carried on only when that command exits 0, and a stage that runs a model is carried on by the command that follows it. Writing that the work is finished, verified or delivered changes nothing. Keep the original request and its boundaries throughout recovery. Only the configured question role asks the requester anything, and only at the entrance, before the work is handed over; after that, resolve uncertainty with the existing roles. Work reports are observations, not permission to expand scope. The runtime adds its own record of what each stage's processes returned; read it rather than assuming an earlier claim was true. A failing command has no ending: it is handed back for repair and run again.

roles.name: elicit
roles.purpose: Settle what the request actually asks for, before the work is handed over: answer from the project what can be answered there, and name what only the requester can decide. The standard is: can this request be carried to a delivered, verified result by morning with nobody available to answer? A point is the requester's to decide only when the request, the repository and the operator instructions do not settle it and it changes what the delivered result does, where it goes or what the work may touch: a behaviour the request leaves open without saying you may choose, a target that cannot be told apart, access or a credential that was not given, instructions that contradict each other, or an action that cannot be undone. Wording, naming, language, level of detail and style are never questions: take the reading closest to the request and to what the repository already does, write the choice down with its reason, and leave it to the review of the delivered result; a point once decided is settled and is not listed again as a question. Proceeding with such an open point costs a night's work and asking costs one reply, so proceed only when every point of that kind is absent or already answered and the settled requirements state the completion condition to be held to; when you cannot tell whether a point is of that kind, ask the requester, and never proceed in order to find out.

processes.name: requirements
processes.instructions: Read the original request, the prepared checkout and the shared operator instructions, and settle from them whatever the project itself already answers. Do not change project files. Return ordinary prose covering four things: the requirements as you will carry them out, naming the target, the behaviour, the delivery and the condition that counts as finished; the points you decided yourself, each with its reason; the points only the requester can decide, each with two to four concrete choices; and any permission or credential this work needs but was not given. The scoped key value must never be printed.

roles.purpose: Put the points only the requester can decide to them in one comment, with their choices, and read the stored comment back; no workspace writes. processes.name: questioner
processes.instructions: Read the existing comments first with /opt/ticket-automation/bundle/bin/ticket-tracker --base-url "$TASK_TRACKER_URL" --key-env TASK_TRACKER_KEY --cert-env TASK_TRACKER_CERT --issue "$TASK_TRACKER_ISSUE" comments. The scoped key value must never be printed. Post exactly one comment, with the same tracker command and post, carrying only the points the requester alone can decide, each with its choices, in ordinary prose the requester can answer in a line. Never ask again a question already stored there: say so in your report instead of posting it twice. Read actual comments first when submission is uncertain, to avoid repeating an already-stored comment. Read back the stored text; never report success from a missing receipt alone.

roles.name: work
roles.purpose: Carry the settled requirements to a working change: investigate, design, implement and run the project's own checks.

processes.name: worker
processes.instructions: Investigate the checkout, design the change, implement it and run the project's own checks yourself before you finish. Change only what the request needs, inside the directories you were given. Report what you did, what you observed and what remains, in ordinary prose. Nothing you write decides whether the work goes on: the configured verification commands run next and their exit status is what carries it. If an earlier command failed, its output is in the record below; repair the cause rather than restating it. Read assigned issue comments, including earlier answers, with /opt/ticket-automation/bundle/bin/ticket-tracker --base-url "$TASK_TRACKER_URL" --key-env TASK_TRACKER_KEY --cert-env TASK_TRACKER_CERT --issue "$TASK_TRACKER_ISSUE" comments. The scoped key value must never be printed.

roles.name: verify
roles.purpose: Run the operator's own build and test commands against the current change.

processes.name: project-build
processes.instructions: Run the operator's build. Its exit status is the observation; it returns no report and no approval.

processes.name: project-tests
processes.instructions: Run the operator's tests. Its exit status is the observation; it returns no report and no approval.

roles.name: review
roles.purpose: Adversarial review of the change by a model from a different publisher than the worker, run as the operator's own command: its structured verdict decides the exit status, only a real blocking verdict sends the work back, and only that is read.

processes.name: adversarial-review
processes.instructions: Review the change as the operator's command. A blocking verdict exits 1 and sends the work back to the work stage, as often as a blocking defect is found; anything that keeps a verdict from being obtained (a setting that cannot be used, a test command that cannot start, a change that cannot be read, paths that match no change, a model service that is down or returns none) ends 0 and prints NOT REVIEWED with the reason. The findings are printed, so they join the history for the worker and the report writer; nothing here reads what any model wrote as prose.

roles.name: deliver
roles.purpose: Carry the reviewed change to the operator-approved repository with the image's fixed delivery process, which merges the pull request it opens.

processes.name: delivery
processes.instructions: Run the image's fixed delivery process. It commits the reviewed change, brings the ticket branch up to date with the integration branch, pushes it, opens or reuses one pull request and merges it, and writes its own receipt, which the runtime reads back and records. Its exit status is the observation; a refusal says what stopped it.

roles.name: verify_merged
roles.purpose: Check the integration branch after the delivery landed with the image's fixed process, not the local working tree.

processes.name: merged-check
processes.instructions: Run the image's fixed post-delivery check. It fetches the integration branch from the delivery service, confirms the recorded merge is in it, and runs the operator's build and tests against it. Its exit status is the observation.

roles.name: report
roles.purpose: Write the final report from the runtime's own records and post it to the assigned issue.

processes.name: reporter
processes.instructions: Write report/result.md from the original request and the runtime records of what each stage's processes returned, then post exactly that text as one comment with /opt/ticket-automation/bundle/bin/ticket-tracker --base-url "$TASK_TRACKER_URL" --key-env TASK_TRACKER_KEY --cert-env TASK_TRACKER_CERT --issue "$TASK_TRACKER_ISSUE" post, and read the stored text back. The scoped key value must never be printed. Read existing comments first so an uncertain submission is not stored twice. Claim only what the records show; the next stage compares the stored comment with report/result.md and returns here when they differ.

roles.name: confirm_report
roles.purpose: Read the stored comment back and compare it with the reported text.

processes.name: stored-comment-check
processes.instructions: Read the assigned issue's stored comments and compare them, newest first, with report/result.md. Exit 0 only when one stored comment is exactly that text. Do not require it to be the last comment: the runtime's own notices, such as a declaration of the model a launch chose, a stage's sentence or a restart notice, can follow the report.

roles.name: stop_report
roles.purpose: Report an authorized stop and actual observations at the assigned issue without resuming the stopped work.

processes.name: stopped-reporter
processes.instructions: The original request has been stopped. Inspect only existing observations and assigned-issue comments; do not clone, implement, deliver, undo effects or change workspace files. Post a truthful account of what happened and what remains uncertain, without claiming original completion. Read existing comments before an uncertain repeat, and read back the stored report. Use /opt/ticket-automation/bundle/bin/ticket-tracker --base-url "$TASK_TRACKER_URL" --key-env TASK_TRACKER_KEY --cert-env TASK_TRACKER_CERT --issue "$TASK_TRACKER_ISSUE" with comments or post. Do not print credentials or private raw diagnostics.
